### ISSUE-073 worked around, not fixed (as instructed)
Every `ship-merge-decision` probe was passed the **bare** PR number — `--pr 121`, `--pr 123`, `--pr 122` — never the issues.md `PR:` field. All three returned `{"action": "merge"}` before any merge, so no merge was ever attempted twice and no force-push happened anywhere in the phase. ISSUE-066's compound `PR: #122 https://…/pull/122` field was deliberately **left un-normalized**: it is one of only two live instances of that shape (ISSUE-062/PR #108 is the other) and ISSUE-073 carries an AC forcing an explicit normalize-vs-refuse decision over exactly that census — quietly normalizing one instance would erode the evidence and could make the defect look already handled.

- [iter 1, review triage] **The ISSUE-074 contract gap, in detail** (attested at four sites, found by the planner while working around it): the team-lead contract states "all `issues.md` modifications go through planner + `flock_edit.sh`", but `agents/planner.md` grants `tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Write, Edit` with **no Bash**, so the planner structurally cannot run the lock wrapper it is instructed to use. It correctly refused to edit `issues.md` directly and instead emitted idempotent apply scripts for the team-lead to run under the lock — the right call, but the contract and the toolset disagree. This is review lesson 9 ("allowed-tools grants map to real call sites") pointing at the kit's own agent roster. Attested at four sites: `agents/team-lead.md:165` (+ :18, :252) forbids team-lead writes; `agents/planner.md:126-127` tells the planner to use `flock_edit.sh` itself; `agents/planner.md:4` gives it no Bash. Asymmetry worth noting: `scripts/preambles.py:85-93` injects the same `registry_edit.sh` pattern into **skill** preambles, which run where Bash exists — so the instruction is satisfiable there; the gap is specific to the **agent** layer, which is also the layer every `issues.md` write is routed through.
  - **The obvious fix is the wrong one, and ISSUE-074 records why.** "Just grant the planner `Bash(bash scripts/flock_edit.sh:*)`" looks like a narrow, lesson-9-compliant grant — but team-lead verified the wrappers execute arbitrary argv (`scripts/flock_edit.sh:29,83` and `scripts/registry_edit.sh:30` all run `"$@"`, and the documented call form is `-- bash -c '<cmd>'`). That grant is therefore **arbitrary code execution behind a narrow-looking prefix**: it satisfies the letter of the allowed-tools lesson while voiding its intent. ISSUE-074 selects the other fix — planner *prepares*, a Bash-capable caller *commits* under the lock — which matches the six applies performed today and needs no new grant (team-lead already has Bash at `agents/team-lead.md:4`). The narrow grant becomes defensible only alongside a new non-exec'ing content-only wrapper, recorded in the issue as the follow-up path.
  - Handoff shape the issue prescribes (the one that worked six times today): planner-authored **idempotent** apply scripts carrying an `### ISSUE-NNN:` anchor guard, run by a Bash-capable caller under `registry_edit.sh`. The guard is part of the contract — an unguarded re-run is itself a duplicate-registry-entry bug.

## Team-lead pre-review leads (handed to the review sub-tasks as leads, NOT conclusions — each reviewer must verify independently)
- ISSUE-068 (A) huge-ID `int()`: the two new `int(match.group(1))` calls are the ONLY int-casts on issue IDs in sprint_queue.py. Concrete crash mechanism supplied: CPython 3.11+ `sys.int_max_str_digits` (default 4300) makes `int("1"*4301)` raise ValueError, which would be an uncaught crash in the LIVE sprint engine. Cheapest fix if judged reachable: bound the regex (`\d{1,9}`), not a try/except.
- ISSUE-068 (B) quadratic dep rebuild: confirmed loop-invariant set comprehension inside the per-row loop in `compute_queues`; severity to be calibrated to real scale (~68 issues).

Reviewer tasked with proving EQUIVALENCE + test-pinning (delete each control, a test must fail), not mere presence.
- ISSUE-067 (C) highest-value: main's `decide_gate_path` docstring promised "Prints nothing on the dormant flavors (stdout stays byte-identical)"; the branch REMOVED that sentence — an intentional contract break (silence was the bug). ## Review findings — what the reviewers actually settled (leads above were confirmed, refuted, or refined)
- **ISSUE-068 (A) CONFIRMED and FIXED.** Both new `int()` sites crash on an `ISSUE-<4301 digits>` cell with no JSON on stdout, while main handles the same fixtures fine — a live-engine regression. Fixed with a bounded `_ROSTER_ID_RE` (`\d{1,9}`), mutation-verified (reverting to `\d+` fails all three new tests).
- **ISSUE-068 (B) CONFIRMED, not fixed (Low).** Measured: 68 issues / 3 unrostered = 0.028 ms; 4000/2000 = 480 ms. Quadratic is real, cost is microseconds at any plausible scale. Recorded as `[shrink]` minimality.
- **ISSUE-068 (C) lesson-8 scoping CONFIRMED SOUND.** All five mutations caught, none hollow; the `unrostered` flag is unforgeable from markdown. One structural note: no *pre-existing* legacy test fails when the flag is forced always-True, so byte-identity rests on the single dedicated pin added by the same PR.
- **ISSUE-068 — a second High the leads did not anticipate, FIXED:** discovery was *starving the STUCK escalation*. `choose_action` checks `implement_ready` before `in_flight`, so a synthesized row converted `STUCK` (issue wedged at `shipping`, attempts=2 — the ISSUE-052 crash window) into `PIPELINE` on new work; and because synthesized rows rebuild `attempts: "0"` every call, the starvation had **no terminating counter** — Attempts froze and the >=3 human escalation could never fire. Fixed by withholding synthesized ids while `in_flight` is non-empty.
- **ISSUE-068 — one reviewer fix correctly REVERTED.** A "tolerate annotated Board `Status`" loosening made both gates fail open (`backlog (blocked — do NOT dispatch)` became admissible; `done (security sign-off still pending)` resolved a dependency) — the mirror image of this issue's own motivating harm. The security dimension caught it; reverted, net code change zero, value retained as `TestAnnotatedBoardStatusFailsClosed`.
- **ISSUE-067 (A) hardening EQUIVALENT and genuinely pinned.** Each of the five controls was mutated; every one fails >=1 test (whitelist 4, containment 3, truncation 2, cap 1, O_NOFOLLOW 2). Announcement mutations fail 10 each direction; the clean path asserts `stdout == ""` in four places.
- **ISSUE-067 (B) CONFIRMED a real gap, FIXED.** The containment/mkdir ORDER was correct but pinned by zero tests — swapping the two statements passed 116 tests and was proven exploitable (symlinked `.claude` + absent `runs/` created `<outside>/runs`), because existing fixtures symlinked to an already-existing dir where `mkdir(exist_ok=True)` no-ops. New test added; the swap now fails exactly that test.
- **ISSUE-067 (C) VERDICT: the test diffs are HONEST contract updates, not guard weakenings.** `TestDormantPathsStaySilent` → `TestDormantPathsPrintNoGateOutput` replaced `out == ""` with assertions *strictly stronger in information content* (line count == 1, prefix, knob name, `"GATE" not in out`, plus the event field), and those are mutation-live. One genuine relaxation recorded as Medium: the byte-identity pin gained `setenv(KIT_RUN_ID)`, so it now holds only under a run id the kit never produces.
- **ISSUE-067 (D/E) as predicted:** the stale byte-identity sentence is record-only; the `.claude/run/` vs `.claude/runs/` false alarm was correctly not acted on.
- **ISSUE-067 — emit-site audit independently verified complete.** Exactly two JSONL appenders repo-wide (`kit_telemetry.py` migrated, `project/.claude/hooks/agent_state.py` justified); all five prose emit sites migrated. No site missed. **No eval-gate resurrection** (scope amendment respected).

Ship should either mark it `done` with the follow-up issues explicitly referenced as carrying the unmet ACs, or hold it `waiting`. Closing it silently on the delivered content would be false. ISSUE-066's rebase onto `kit_telemetry.emit_event` is NOT the "one function body swap" SPEC-066 assumed.** 067 deliberately replaced silent-skip with announce semantics, so **two ISSUE-066 tests pin the opposite contract and must be rewritten**: `tests/test_review_context.py:304` (`test_unset_run_id_is_silent_noop_exit_0`) and `:320` (`test_invalid_run_id_refused`, asserts the runs dir is empty) — 067 writes `unattributed.jsonl` + a `run_id_fallback` field + one stdout line in both cases. **6. NEW — team-lead independently verified a LIVE defect that affects THIS sprint's ship phase: ISSUE-066's `PR:` field is unparseable by the ISSUE-052 merge probe, so its FINALIZE crash-recovery is DEAD.**
- `scripts/sprint_queue.py` parses the Board `PR:` field as `pr_raw.strip()` with **zero validation** and passes it to `gh pr view <pr_ref>` as a **bare positional** (line 228 — the only `gh` call in the file).
- The implement phase wrote the three PR fields in **two different formats**: ISSUE-067 and ISSUE-068 got `https://github.com/pillip/claude-dev-kit/pull/{123,121}` (single token, works), but **ISSUE-066 got `#122 https://github.com/pillip/claude-dev-kit/pull/122`** — a TWO-token value.
- Verified live: `gh pr view '#122 https://…/pull/122' --json state,mergedAt` → `no pull requests found for branch "#122 https://…"`. The probe then hits its non-zero-exit branch and **silently falls back to a phase-only decision**.
- **Precise blast radius (verified, deliberately not overstated — two different extractors read the same field):**
  - `scripts/verify_checkpoint.py::_extract_pr_number` uses `re.search(r"(\d+)\s*$", pr_field)` — trailing digits only — so it extracts `122` correctly. **All ship-phase checkpoints (`checks`, `merge`, `smoke`, `cleanup`) are IMMUNE and work normally.**
  - Only `sprint_queue.py`'s ISSUE-052 FINALIZE merge probe passes the field **raw** and therefore degrades to phase-only for ISSUE-066.
  - Net consequence: for a reviewed-but-already-merged ISSUE-066, `next-action` would propose **SHIP instead of FINALIZE**. That is a *degraded* recovery, not a broken one — the SHIP handler's own `ship-merge-decision` guard still prevents a double merge **provided it is called with the extracted PR number (`122`), not the raw field**. Orchestrator: pass the number.
- **Optional pre-ship tidy (low urgency, now that the blast radius is known):** normalize ISSUE-066's `PR:` field to the single-URL form so it matches 067/068. Nice-to-have, not a ship blocker.
- This is still the sprint's own theme (an instrument degrading silently) reproduced inside the engine. ISSUE-073 covers it: the planner independently censused the field, found the SAME compound shape on ISSUE-062/PR #108, confirmed `verify_checkpoint.py`'s five `gh` sites are structurally immune, and wrote an AC forcing an explicit **normalize-vs-refuse** decision rather than leaving the compound case undefined.
- **ALSO RELEVANT TO THE SHIP PHASE RUNNING NEXT — a second injection entry point, reachable without touching the Board at all.** `cmd_ship_merge_decision` (`scripts/sprint_queue.py:626`) passes `args.pr` straight into `_gh_pr_merge_state`, and `args.pr` is a **model-chosen CLI argument** supplied per `skills/ship/SKILL.md` step 4 — the same `ship-merge-decision --pr <pr_number>` call the FINALIZE handler and the ship merge step both invoke. So the unvalidated-ref path is live in the ship flow itself, not only in Board parsing. Practical guidance for this sprint's ship: **pass the bare extracted PR number** (`121`, `123`, `122`) to `--pr`, never the raw Board field and never an unvalidated value. ISSUE-073 mandates the guard at the `_gh_pr_merge_state` chokepoint precisely because validating only at the Board-parse site would leave this CLI path open.

**7. Already-uncommitted on main from the implement phase:** `issues.md` (066/067/068 Status/GH-Issue/PR fields + the 067 title/evidence amendment) and `docs/test_plan.md`. Ship's registry finalization needs to fold these in, not clobber them.

## Live validation that arrived for free — ISSUE-068's feature proved itself on real data created during this phase
Filing ISSUE-069..074 produced exactly the condition ISSUE-068 was built for, so the two engines can be compared on genuine data rather than fixtures:
- **main**: `{"action": "SHIP", "targets": [066,067,068], "reason": "3 issue(s) in reviewed status …"}` — **completely silent** about the six new Board issues.
- **ISSUE-068's branch**: same action and targets, plus `"unrostered": ["ISSUE-069",…,"ISSUE-074"]` and a `[visibility: …auto-considered: …]` suffix on the reason.
This is the strongest argument for merging PR #121 despite its unmet ACs: the capability is real and demonstrably not fixture-only, and it is the difference between the orchestrator seeing six P1 follow-ups and not seeing them at all. It also confirms the reviewer's caveat was precise — the earlier byte-identity check was vacuous *for the new path* (no candidates existed then); now that candidates exist, the two engines diverge exactly as designed, and only in the annotation.

**And the ISSUE-069 ratchet hazard is now LIVE on this very backlog.** The watermark is currently `max(066,067,068) = 68`, so all six follow-ups sit above it and are visible. But they are all P1, so ordering among them is not ID-ordered — **if ISSUE-074 is rostered before ISSUE-069..073, the watermark becomes 74 and those five silently vanish** (no target, no `unrostered`, no `stranded`). Until ISSUE-069 lands, the orchestrator should roster these six in **ascending ID order**, or roster them all at once, and should not trust `DONE` while any of them is outstanding.
